snapshot.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (NYSE: TSM ) remains the biggest beneficiary of the artificial intelligence semiconductor boom, with analysts at Counterpoint Research expecting its growth to accelerate through the second half of 2026 as advanced-node demand and packaging capacity remain tight. Counterpoint said Taiwan Semiconductor’s revenue rose 34% year over year and 12% sequentially to $40.2 billion in the second quarter. That gave the company about 42% of the broader Foundry 2.0 market, up from 38% in 2025. The research firm expects Taiwan Semiconductor’s full-year 2026 revenue to grow about 43%, implying growth of nearly 50% in the second half. AI Demand Keeps Taiwan Semiconductor at the Center Counterpoint Associate Director Brady Wang said the AI investment cycle has broadened across pure-play foundries, non-memory chipmakers and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test companies. However, he said Taiwan Semiconductor remains the “central beneficiary.” The firm estimates Taiwan Semiconductor’s CoWoS advanced-packaging supply-demand gap at about 20% in 2026. It expects the shortfall to narrow to roughly 10% in 2027 as in-house capacity expands toward 185,000 wafers per month. Counterpoint said Taiwan Semiconductor’s second-half growth will depend on the ramp of its N2 process, wafer price increases and planned CoWoS capacity additions. Tight packaging capacity is currently limiting AI product shipments, prompting Taiwan Semiconductor to increase back-end investment while customers develop alternative packaging options. See More: Top Value Stocks Samsung, Intel Gain As Customers Seek Alternatives Senior Analyst William Li said Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (OTC: SSNLF ) and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC ) are also benefiting as customers look for additional manufacturing sources. Samsung held the No. 2 foundry position with about 4% market share during the quarter, supported by SF4 and SF5 demand and higher wafer prices. Intel, meanwhile, has gained traction with its EMIB-T packaging technology, which has been adopted for Google’s next-generation TPU, according to Counterpoint. Still, Li said neither company currently matches Taiwan Semiconductor’s combination of advanced-node scale, manufacturing yields and packaging execution. AI Boom Broadens Across Chip Supply Chain The broader Foundry 2.0 market reached a record $96.6 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 25% from a year earlier and 11% sequentially. Counterpoint attributed the growth to demand for AI GPUs, custom ASICs, server CPUs, networking chips and power-management semiconductors. Non-Taiwan Semiconductor pure-play foundry revenue rose 18% year over year. Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. led that group with 36% growth, helped by demand for domestic AI chips in China. Hua Hong and Nexchip posted growth of 17% and 21%, respectively. Meanwhile, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test revenue rose 22% to $12.6 billion. ASE Technology posted 24% growth, while Amkor Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMKR ) grew 26%, as advanced packaging, wafer probing and AI processor testing demand strengthened. Counterpoint expects the Foundry 2.0 market to maintain double-digit growth through the second half of 2026. However, it flagged CoWoS and substrate shortages, higher wafer and packaging costs, weak consumer demand and trade-policy uncertainty as key risks. TSM Price Action: Taiwan Semiconductor shares were down 0.49% at $454.72 during premarket trading on Wednesday, according to Benzinga Pro data . Photo via Shutterstock

criterion: Intel客户端供给约束缓解后，季度客户端单位同比达到不下降，且头部OEM或覆盖性渠道确认终端sell-through带来补单而库存未增加。

criterion: Acer、ASUS、Dell、HP、Lenovo或Samsung中的单一头部OEM确认Core Ultra Series 3量产机型已产生终端销售，并据此补单或扩大生产组合。
policies.match_scope: 召回Googlebook及其他头部OEM的Core Series 3机型、量产上市、终端销售、渠道库存、补单、组合扩张及取消消息。

policies.match_scope: 召回边缘AI、机器人、Core Ultra/Core Series 3的测试、量产design win、采购批次、现场部署、扩展与终止消息。

criterion: 重要边缘AI或机器人测试客户明确终止Intel项目，或在量产版本中选择替代芯片并移除或减少Intel内容。
policies.match_scope: 召回边缘AI/机器人客户的Intel测试、量产设计选择、BOM、替代芯片、项目终止和Intel内容变化消息。

criterion: Intel季度报告客户端总单位同比仍下降，同时明确客户端收入改善主要来自约10%提价或高端SKU mix，而非单位增长。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel客户端收入、单位、ASP、约10%提价、高端/主流SKU mix和sell-through的财报与渠道消息。

criterion: Intel或头部OEM确认客户端生产批次因晶圆、封装或基板优先分配给服务器、AI或高端SKU而被延期、缩量或取消。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel客户端晶圆/封装/基板分配、服务器/AI优先级、OEM短缺、交付延期、缩量和取消消息。

criterion: 有管辖权的政府发布最终且已生效或确定生效日的跨境限制，直接禁止Intel客户端产品或关键投入进入重大市场，或迫使头部OEM取消/重配生产机型。
policies.match_scope: 召回出口管制、关税、地区限制、海关实施、Intel PC/边缘产品、关键投入和OEM区域配置调整消息。

criterion: 单一重大云或企业客户将Xeon 6或18A基础Xeon 6+从验证推进为有约束力的非AI生产采购/部署或下一代生产续约。
policies.match_scope: 召回Xeon 6/6+的企业与云非AI生产平台、客户采购、部署、续约、验证、设计胜负及取消消息。

policies.match_scope: 召回Xeon 6/6+的良率、周期时间、软件验证、客户认证、量产、上市、交付窗口和取消消息。

criterion: Intel、后端伙伴或客户确认可识别的重大非AI Xeon生产订单因封装、基板、测试或系统集成不足而延期、降配或无法履约。
policies.match_scope: 召回非AI Xeon订单、封装、基板、测试、系统集成、填充率、交付周期、延期和取消消息。

policies.match_scope: 召回AMD EPYC/Arm等服务器CPU供给、重大企业/云客户的Xeon非AI采购、续约、扩量、平台分配与取消消息。

criterion: 替代CPU供给恢复后，单一重大企业或云客户在下一轮非AI生产平台中取消或削减Xeon，并转向AMD、Arm/RISC-V或自研CPU。
policies.match_scope: 召回替代服务器CPU供给、重大客户非AI平台、Xeon设计输单、采购转移、订单取消和平台更新消息。

criterion: 重大数据中心生产平台的新一代架构相对前代明确减少每系统Xeon数量、移除Xeon工作负载或迁移至加速器/自研芯片。
policies.match_scope: 召回数据中心平台BOM、每系统CPU数量、工作负载迁移、Xeon内容、加速器和自研芯片的前后代配置变化。

criterion: Intel确认覆盖物质需求的企业/云客户群因预算、TCO、虚拟化效率或库存把已计划非AI Xeon刷新后移，并削减或暂停对应近期订单。
policies.match_scope: 召回企业/云服务器刷新、Xeon订单、backlog、预算、TCO、虚拟化效率、库存、延期和恢复消息。

criterion: 单一主要云客户将下一代非AI生产平台中原由Xeon承载的工作负载迁至自研CPU或单一替代供应商，并减少或停止Intel部署。
policies.match_scope: 召回主要云客户的自研CPU、非AI实例、生产平台迁移、Xeon内容、采购集中、部署停止及维持Intel平台的消息。

criterion: Intel确认服务器供给约束实质缓解后，同一季度服务器单位同比增速不高于9%，且ASP同比增速从48%基线显著回落或转负。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel服务器供给缓解、季度单位同比、ASP同比、高端mix、毛利桥及供需正常化后的价格变化。

criterion: Intel在Q3及Q4 FY2026两个连续季度同时披露良率或周期时间改善、合格单位/利用率改善，且毛利或营业利润桥主要由经营变量而非重组费用下降驱动。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel连续季度良率、周期时间、合格单位、利用率、毛利桥、营业利润和重组费用贡献的财报及制造更新。

criterion: Intel确认18A-P、High-NA或后续先进节点量产良率下降、缺陷/返工/报废上升或周期时间拉长，并识别合格产出下降或毛利桥中的爬坡成本。
policies.match_scope: 召回18A-P、High-NA及后续节点的良率、缺陷、返工、报废、周期时间、good wafers、客户资格和爬坡成本消息。

policies.match_scope: 召回Intel Foundry报告收入、外部客户收入、内部交易、利用率、经营亏损、分部抵销和合并毛利桥。

policies.match_scope: 召回Intel外部Foundry客户、节点资格、tape-out、正式订单、产能预订、付费晶圆/封装和合格生产消息。

criterion: Intel明确将人员或产品削减直接联系到一项重大产品/节点的验证、工艺支持、良率改善、客户认证、质量或交付延期。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel裁员、R&D/MG&A、产品精简、验证、工艺支持、良率、客户认证、质量与交付延期消息。

criterion: Intel后续单季重组及其他费用或新减值超过10亿美元，并在GAAP营业利润或EPS桥中形成可识别拖累。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel重组及其他费用、减值、股权薪酬、GAAP/非GAAP对账、营业利润和EPS影响。

criterion: Intel正式提价或重订合同后，单一重大客户明确延迟、取消或降配采购，且Intel确认价格收益被销量、mix或利用率损失抵消。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel PC、服务器和定制产品提价、合同重订、OEM/云客户订单、降配、取消、库存、单位与利用率消息。

criterion: Intel或覆盖物质订单池的主要云/企业客户群或PC OEM群明确取消或实质后移部署/采购，并削减近期Intel订单。
policies.match_scope: 召回云/企业AI资本开支、PC OEM采购、部署取消或延期、Intel订单池、库存、单位出货和利用率消息。

criterion: 有管辖权的政府发布最终且已生效或确定生效日的规则，直接禁止/限制Intel物质产品向重大市场交付，或对关键制造投入施加不可规避的物质成本。
policies.match_scope: 召回出口管制、关税、国家安全审查、公共采购、海关实施、Intel CPU/AI产品、关键投入及订单/成本影响。

criterion: Intel或单一重大客户确认重大可靠性、安全或质量问题已导致重要产品资格暂停、召回、返工或shipment hold。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel服务器、PC和先进节点产品的可靠性、安全、erratum、资格暂停、召回、返工、退货和shipment hold。

criterion: Intel报告Q3 FY2026同口径合并收入低于158亿美元。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel Q3 FY2026合并收入、158亿美元指引下限、供给/制造缺口、客户延迟取消、库存去化和替代架构归因。

criterion: Intel报告Q3 FY2026同口径合并收入高于168亿美元。

policies.match_scope: 召回Intel Q3收入、GAAP/non-GAAP毛利率、组合、利用率、良率、节点及封装/基板成本桥。

criterion: Intel报告Q3 GAAP毛利率高于41%且非GAAP毛利率高于42%，并将超额主要归因于良率、周期时间、合格单位、利用率或产品组合改善。

Intel Q3收入不低于158亿美元且毛利接近指引，但非GAAP EPS低于0.38美元，差异主要来自费用、税率、稀释股数或调整项目。

policies.match_scope: 召回Intel Q3收入指引、158亿至168亿美元原区间、8-K、预告、撤回和正式更新。

criterion: Intel在Q3业绩报告前正式将GAAP毛利率指引下调至41%以下、将非GAAP毛利率指引下调至42%以下，或撤回任一毛利率指引。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel Q3 GAAP/non-GAAP毛利率41%/42%原指引、8-K、预告、撤回和正式更新。

criterion: Intel在Q3业绩报告前正式将GAAP EPS指引下调至0.31美元以下、将非GAAP EPS指引下调至0.38美元以下，或撤回任一EPS指引。
policies.match_scope: 召回Intel Q3 GAAP/non-GAAP EPS 0.31/0.38美元原指引、8-K、预告、撤回和正式更新。

criterion: 单一重大外部商业客户完成14A tape-out或硅后验证，并签署包含交付窗口或数量范围的有约束力节点级订单/产能预订。

policies.match_scope: 召回18A-P、14A、High-NA的良率、周期时间、掩模/设备吞吐、客户starts、资格和HVM窗口变化。

criterion: 已完成Intel先进节点资格或预订的单一重大客户取消或实质削减Intel节点级booking，并将对应量产明确转向竞争代工或内部工厂。
policies.match_scope: 召回已资格/预订客户的Intel节点booking、生产份额、取消、缩量、TSMC/Samsung/内部制造转移和双源状态。

criterion: Terafab相关方或另一家超大客户与Intel签署指名14A、包含产能/数量或预付款并设交付/量产窗口的不可取消商业制造协议。

policies.match_scope: 召回先进节点设备、掩模、材料、供应中断、出口/安全/贸易规则、外部客户starts、产能配给和生产地点迁移。

snapshot.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd. (NYSE: TSM ) remains the biggest beneficiary of the artificial intelligence semiconductor boom, with analysts at Counterpoint Research expecting its growth to accelerate through the second half of 2026 as advanced-node demand and packaging capacity remain tight. Counterpoint said Taiwan Semiconductor’s revenue rose 34% year over year and 12% sequentially to $40.2 billion in the second quarter. That gave the company about 42% of the broader Foundry 2.0 market, up from 38% in 2025. The research firm expects Taiwan Semiconductor’s full-year 2026 revenue to grow about 43%, implying growth of nearly 50% in the second half. AI Demand Keeps Taiwan Semiconductor at the Center Counterpoint Associate Director Brady Wang said the AI investment cycle has broadened across pure-play foundries, non-memory chipmakers and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test companies. However, he said Taiwan Semiconductor remains the “central beneficiary.” The firm estimates Taiwan Semiconductor’s CoWoS advanced-packaging supply-demand gap at about 20% in 2026. It expects the shortfall to narrow to roughly 10% in 2027 as in-house capacity expands toward 185,000 wafers per month. Counterpoint said Taiwan Semiconductor’s second-half growth will depend on the ramp of its N2 process, wafer price increases and planned CoWoS capacity additions. Tight packaging capacity is currently limiting AI product shipments, prompting Taiwan Semiconductor to increase back-end investment while customers develop alternative packaging options. See More: Top Value Stocks Samsung, Intel Gain As Customers Seek Alternatives Senior Analyst William Li said Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (OTC: SSNLF ) and Intel Corp. (NASDAQ: INTC ) are also benefiting as customers look for additional manufacturing sources. Samsung held the No. 2 foundry position with about 4% market share during the quarter, supported by SF4 and SF5 demand and higher wafer prices. Intel, meanwhile, has gained traction with its EMIB-T packaging technology, which has been adopted for Google’s next-generation TPU, according to Counterpoint. Still, Li said neither company currently matches Taiwan Semiconductor’s combination of advanced-node scale, manufacturing yields and packaging execution. AI Boom Broadens Across Chip Supply Chain The broader Foundry 2.0 market reached a record $96.6 billion in second-quarter revenue, up 25% from a year earlier and 11% sequentially. Counterpoint attributed the growth to demand for AI GPUs, custom ASICs, server CPUs, networking chips and power-management semiconductors. Non-Taiwan Semiconductor pure-play foundry revenue rose 18% year over year. Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp. led that group with 36% growth, helped by demand for domestic AI chips in China. Hua Hong and Nexchip posted growth of 17% and 21%, respectively. Meanwhile, outsourced semiconductor assembly and test revenue rose 22% to $12.6 billion. ASE Technology posted 24% growth, while Amkor Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMKR ) grew 26%, as advanced packaging, wafer probing and AI processor testing demand strengthened. Counterpoint expects the Foundry 2.0 market to maintain double-digit growth through the second half of 2026. However, it flagged CoWoS and substrate shortages, higher wafer and packaging costs, weak consumer demand and trade-policy uncertainty as key risks.
